gap: No result ChatGPT got states that light makers' manuals disagree on chemistry: Costco's SL-1001-8PK (GTX) manual forbids NiCd and calls for 1.2 V 1,000 mAh NiMH only, and Hampton Bay's 84101 manual calls for 1.2 V 900 mAh NiMH. On the battery side, Tenergy states its Solla Premium is not a replacement for LiFePO4 cells, and XTAR states its 1.5 V lithium AA needs about 5 V to charge and works only in listed XTAR chargers, so a solar light can't recharge it.
standout_why: I compared against these pages. idealgardenlights.com (cited) says only to match voltage and use the light maker's recommended cells. It gives no light-by-light specs and doesn't mention 1.5 V lithium AA. power.tenergy.com Solla 1000 (cited) states no exclusions. solarpatiolights.net covers part of it: it says some makers allow NiMH in a NiCd light and others don't, and it cites a Harbor Breeze manual that requires NiCd only. But it doesn't mention any manual that bans NiCd (Costco GTX), the Solla Premium LiFePO4 exclusion, or the ~5 V charge requirement of 1.5 V lithium AA. ChatGPT's answer says '1.2V (not 1.5V lithium-ion)' but gives no reason and no source.
decides: This confirms the pick of 1.2 V NiMH, and the Tenergy Solla 1000 mAh is an exact match for the Costco GTX spec (1.2 V 1,000 mAh NiMH, NiCd banned). The page should send readers to the battery line in their own light's manual, because chemistry rules differ by brand: Costco bans NiCd, and the Harbor Breeze manual quoted by solarpatiolights.net requires NiCd. Lights that came with 3.2 V LiFePO4 cells need a different battery, which Tenergy states for the Solla Premium. 1.5 V lithium AA such as the XTAR 4150 mWh, which Dealectric lists, should be marked as not for solar lights.

findings.label: Required battery and exclusions in the light maker's manual
findings.value: Only AA 1.2 V 1,000 mAh NiMH. 'Do not use alkaline, standard (carbon-zinc) or NiCd (nickel cadmium) batteries in GTX solar lights.' 'Do not mix battery types.'
findings.source_title: Costco SL-1001-8PK Care And Use Instructions, page 2 (ManualsLib)
findings.note: Quoted from the battery-information section of the care-and-use manual. Same spec as the Tenergy Solla 1000 mAh.

findings.label: Required replacement battery in the light maker's manual
findings.value: One 1.2 V NiMH AA, 900 mAh. Manual says to replace it every 3 years.
findings.note: 'CAUTION: When replacing the battery, use one (1) 1.2V Ni_Mh AA 900mAh rechargeable battery.' The manual doesn't say whether NiCd or alkaline is prohibited.

findings.label: Stated compatibility and exclusion
findings.value: Tenergy calls it an 'ideal replacement' for NiCd or NiMH solar batteries and states it is 'NOT a replacement for LifePO4 batteries'.
findings.source_title: Tenergy Solla Premium Rechargeable NiMH AA Battery, 1300mAh, 12 PCS - Tenergy Power
findings.note: Maker's US product page. 1.2 V NiMH, 2,000 cycles, -4 to 122 °F, ships precharged.

findings.label: Price (P/N 19043)
findings.value: $18.99 (title says 12-pack, but the spec list says '8 x AA Rechargeable Batteries')
findings.source_title: Tenergy Solla Premium Rechargeable NiMH AA Battery, 1300mAh, 12 PCS - Tenergy Power
findings.note: The page contradicts itself on pack count. Our current row says '12 (8 for $14.49)', which doesn't match today's page and needs updating.

findings.label: Spec, price and stated compatibility (P/N 19035)
findings.value: 1.2 V NiMH 1,000 mAh, 2,000 cycles, -4 to 122 °F. $16.99 for 12, $25.99 for 24 (P/N 19036). 'Specifically designed for solar lights.' No exclusions stated.
findings.source_title: Tenergy Solla AA Rechargeable NiMH AA Battery, 1000mAh, 12 PCS, UL Certified
findings.note: Maker's US store. The page lists no light models it fits and gives no NiCd or LiFePO4 statement.

findings.label: Charging requirement and compatible chargers
findings.value: Needs about 5 V to charge (3.6 V cell with a step-down chip inside). XTAR lists only its VX4, MX4, L8, L4, BC8 and BC4 as compatible. The FC2, VC4, VC4SL, VC2SL, VC8, VC8S, VC8 PLUS, VP4L PLUS, VP4 PLUS 'and other models' can't charge it.
findings.source_title: FAQs about XTAR 4150mWh AA Li-ion Battery
findings.note: XTAR doesn't mention solar lights. The point that a solar light's charging circuit can't recharge it is our inference from the maker's ~5 V requirement and its list of compatible chargers. XTAR also says it's unsuitable for clocks and other low-drain devices.

findings.label: What the cited rival says on compatibility
findings.value: 'Only use the manufacturer's recommended rechargeable batteries in your lights.' Li-ion is incompatible with NiCd and NiMH. Wrong voltage 'can damage the solar components.' Do not leave alkaline batteries in the lights.
findings.source_title: Solar Lights Guide - Ideal Garden Lights USA
findings.note: Cited by ChatGPT. Gives no light-by-light battery specs and doesn't mention 1.5 V lithium AA.
